display_name: Canada Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA)
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA) is Part 3 of Canada's Bill C-27 (Digital Charter Implementation Act). It establishes requirements for the responsible design, development, and deployment of AI systems, with particular focus on high-impact systems that may cause significant harm to individuals or their interests.

risk_tiers.description: AI systems that meet criteria prescribed by regulation for high-impact designation. These systems are subject to the full set of AIDA obligations including assessments, mitigation measures, and transparency requirements.
criteria: AI system used in decisions related to employment, including recruitment and termination
AI system determining access to financial services, credit, or insurance
AI system used in healthcare diagnosis, treatment, or prioritization
AI system used in law enforcement, criminal justice, or immigration decisions
AI system that may affect individuals' fundamental rights
AI system used for biometric identification or profiling
AI system managing critical infrastructure operations

risk_tiers.description: AI systems that do not meet high-impact criteria but are still subject to general obligations including record-keeping and prohibition on reckless or malicious use.
criteria: AI systems used in commercial operations not meeting high-impact thresholds
Customer-facing AI systems with moderate individual impact
AI systems used for content generation or recommendation
Internal decision-support tools with human oversight

risk_tiers.description: AI systems with negligible potential for harm to individuals. Subject only to the general prohibition on harmful or deceptive use.
criteria: AI systems used purely for internal analytics
Low-stakes automation with no individual impact
Research and development systems not deployed publicly
AI-assisted tools with full human control over outputs

key_obligations.obligation: Assess whether an AI system is a high-impact system and document the assessment, including potential harms and mitigation measures
Establish measures to identify, assess, and mitigate risks of harm or biased output that could result from the use of the AI system
Monitor compliance with mitigation measures and assess their effectiveness on an ongoing basis throughout the system lifecycle
Publish a plain-language description of the AI system explaining how it is used, the types of decisions it makes, and mitigation measures in place
Maintain records of assessments, mitigation measures, and any incidents or adverse outcomes for prescribed retention periods
Notify the AI and Data Commissioner of material harm or risk of imminent material harm resulting from the AI system

data_residency_requirements: Canada (PIPEDA and provincial privacy laws apply)
enforcement_timeline: Bill C-27 introduced June 2022. AIDA is Part 3 of the bill. As of 2024, the bill remains under parliamentary consideration. Regulations to define high-impact criteria will follow royal assent.
recent_changes: Companion document published with proposed high-impact system criteria
AI and Data Commissioner role proposed for enforcement oversight
Amendments proposed to strengthen individual rights and transparency requirements
